harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured `/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker` as the enabled `inventory-worker` systemd service on node1. It runs under the dedicated locked `inventorysvc` account and recovered successfully after a full node restart. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the `inventorysvc` system account with no home, a locked password, and `/sbin/nologin`.
Installed and enabled a hardened SELinux-labeled `inventory-worker.service` unit.
Verified the running process uses the expected unprivileged UID/GID and has `NoNewPrivileges` enabled.
Restarted node1 safely and verified boot identity changed and the service automatically recovered.
Installed no additional software and left the system healthy with no failed units.

evidence.requirement: Run the worker as managed service `inventory-worker` under `inventorysvc`
evidence.summary: The dedicated account exists; the service is enabled and active; its live process runs with UID/GID 992 matching inventorysvc; the account is locked and uses nologin.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible native service management
evidence.summary: Before and after configuration, node1 reports RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The native systemd unit passes verification.

SELinux remains enforcing; unit and executable labels are correct; the service uses no-new-privileges, an empty capability set, protected filesystems/kernel interfaces, restrictive umask, and restart-on-failure.

Healthy baseline boot ID 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a was captured, reboot acknowledgement returned, post-restart boot ID changed to 0552fbec-93d3-4a3d-b13d-3dc06e94edfb, and the system plus inventory-worker recovered to running/active state.
